name: Crucible IronFist Weld-Chem Work Glove
description: Matte charcoal split-cowhide palm reinforced with para-aramid fiber panels across the knuckles and thumb web. The cuff extends four inches past the wrist with a quick-release buckle, accommodating standard chrome forearm flanges. Stitching is double-locked orange thread — visible wear on older pairs shows gray-white fraying at the finger bases. The back panel is perforated nitrile mesh for heat venting.
functionality: Chemical-splash resistant palm, heat-rated to 400°C at brief contact. Quick-release cuff fits over most standard chrome forearm flanges. Knuckle panels absorb moderate impact. Grip-textured palm performs wet or dry.
what_it_says: You work with your hands and you don't expect the job to be safe.
story_hooks: A pair found at a crime scene still has the corrosive chemical residue — the wrong kind for any legal job site in the district.
The worker wearing these has a chrome right hand she's hiding; the glove's flange slot fits perfectly, but she's been telling her supervisor she's fully organic.
Counterfeit versions are flooding the Shelf market — they look identical but the para-aramid is replaced with cheap polyester, and workers are getting burned.

physical_description.visual_profile: Heavy-duty work glove with industrial presence — matte charcoal palm dominates, contrasting orange stitching catches light, extended cuff reads as utilitarian and protective. Silhouette is blocky at the knuckles, tapers slightly at fingertips. Suggests hands that work with heat and chemicals.
physical_description.fit: Snug through the palm and fingers with structured reinforcement at impact zones. Cuff is generous and straight-cut, designed to sit over or integrate with chrome augmentation flanges without binding. Compression-style across the hand, loose around the wrist opening.
physical_description.primary_material: Split cowhide (palm, inner fingers), para-aramid fiber (knuckle and thumb-web panels), perforated nitrile mesh (back panel and ventilation zones)
physical_description.texture: Matte, slightly weathered cowhide on palm with subtle grain; sharp, tight aramid weave visible on reinforced areas; mesh back has open-grid texture with small circular perforations. Orange stitching sits proud of the surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal matte base with safety-orange double-locked stitching throughout. Nitrile mesh back slightly lighter gray tone. Minimal branding — possible faint GeneFit Health Testing text on cuff interior.
physical_description.closures: Quick-release buckle on cuff extension (likely friction-fit or single-snap design for fast removal in emergency situations)
distinctive_features: Extended four-inch cuff with chrome-flange accommodation notches
Perforated nitrile mesh back panel for heat dissipation
Reinforced knuckle and thumb-web para-aramid panels
Typical wear pattern: gray-white fraying at finger base stitching on aged pairs
No visible logos except internal cuff marking
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional workwear — affordable, durable, designed for repetitive industrial use rather than luxury or salvage
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is hands-on industrial worker — fabrication tech, chemical processor, arc welder, hazmat handler, or medical laboratory technician. GeneFit partnership suggests health-monitoring integration or liability protection. Chrome-flange accommodation signals augmented workforce integration.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in to heavily weathered depending on use. Newer pairs show crisp orange stitching and tight mesh. Older pairs display frayed finger bases, darkened palm stains, mesh compression, possible small burns or chemical spots on cowhide.
